name: The south road into the hills (toward Strahnbrad)
region: Lordaeron, the bending road south from the carters' fork up under the hills, over the shoulder of the hill past the Strahnbrad camp and down to the flat before Andorhal

sensoryProfile.sight: Between hedges, bending out of sight under the hills; cut to pieces by iron-tyred wagons, more coming down than going up; at dawn a long brown moving smear lying along the slope low over the hills, 'too brown for mist'. Chapter 6: mist lying in the road to the mare's knees on the climb, fields and bracken gone grey; out of the mist the hedges stand up sharp with sun on them and bracken rusting on the banks; the road goes over the shoulder of the hill in a cut between two banks with ruts so deep a horse must step down into them and climb out.
sensoryProfile.sound: Chapter 6: iron tyres grinding on stones; a horn and men shouting far up the hill; later a hollow clop of hooves on the culvert stones.
sensoryProfile.smell: Chapter 6: woodsmoke, and under it horses, a great many, more than any farm keeps; dust that tastes of dung at head height.
sensoryProfile.touch: Chapter 6: a dull drag in the road felt through the mare and the staff on every forefoot; it rises at the culvert where a stream runs under the road.
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: The way the grain comes up and the way the army goes. Chapter 6: the road she read heavy all morning, old at the bottom and a thin new layer on top, that carries the army's wagons empty down and loaded up while no one in the camp looks in them.

establishedFacts.fact: Cyndia walked it to the first bridge: heavy wagons with iron tyres, many, both ways, more coming down than going up; the ones coming down ride lighter; the horses are all shod with a wide flat shoe with heavy heel: the King's post-horse shoe seen at the Pass. She judges army wagons, full going up, empty coming down. The road climbs past the bridge into the hills.
Jaina's read: heavy as far down as she can hear; old at the bottom with a new thin layer on top going the same way; the King's road is thin and clean.
Sylvanas's inference: the south road goes through the hills past Strahnbrad and into Andorhal by the back; the army is on it for the orcs.
The party leaves the fork in the old order (Sylvanas, Cyndia left, Lyriel right at Jaina's knee, Jaina centre, two places at the back) and turns south at first light.
Chapter 6: the brown smear Ch5 ended on resolves as dust from army traffic, with smoke rising into it from behind the hill. It lies wider than at first light.
Chapter 6: the road dips to a culvert where a stream runs under it; the drag rises hard there. Beyond it the road climbs out of the mist on the next bend.

Chapter 6: at the top of the cut over the hill the whole Strahnbrad army camp lies on the long slope below, and the road runs down to a huddle of grey roofs where it crosses a stream. Wagons come down empty and go up loaded high under roped tarpaulins; at the foot they turn in behind the cook-tents.

Chapter 6: below Strahnbrad the road runs half empty (an army wagon going up, a boy with a switch driving geese) until the flat, where farm lanes join it and it fills with carts, each lane adding to the drag. It is the way the party reaches Andorhal; it is not the King's road.

eventsHere.event: Chosen as the road to ride; the party enters it at the end of the chapter with an unidentified brown smear over the hills.
Chapter 6: Jaina's plain statement of the plague on the climb; the party meets army wagons; Strahnbrad camp seen from the cut; the afternoon descent to the flat and the Andorhal approach.
